name: backend-architecture
title: Backend architecture and server-side patterns
summary: Structure the Rust server side of a product: the Tokio runtime and process model, workspace layout, monolith and service boundaries, consistency under concurrency, multi-tenancy, background jobs, realtime features, file uploads and resilient third-party integrations.
useWhen: How should I structure the backend: monolith, modules or services?
Spawned Tokio tasks die silently, leak, or never stop on shutdown
Move this slow work to a background job, or add a scheduled job
Jobs are running twice, getting stuck or piling up in the queue
Make this app multi-tenant and keep tenants' data apart
Let customers use their own domain, or keep their data in a chosen region
Add live updates, chat, presence or collaborative editing
Handle file uploads, image processing or CSV import and export
A third-party API being slow or down takes our whole app down
One slow request freezes every other request, or the process drops in-flight requests on SIGTERM

notFor.topic: Endpoint contracts, pagination, API rate limits and generic webhooks
Schema design, transactions, locks and query tuning
Choosing and running Redis, search, object storage or streams
Roles, permissions and per-object access checks
Sending email, SMS and push notifications
Profiling slow endpoints and load testing

references.title: Rust, Tokio and the process model
references.purpose: Read when the server stalls under load, tasks leak or die silently, shutdown drops work, memory keeps growing, or compile times and the Cargo workspace layout slow the team down.

leaves.topic: Keep the Tokio runtime unblocked: spawn_blocking for CPU-heavy or blocking calls
Never hold a std mutex guard across an await; choose the lock deliberately
Supervise spawned tasks with JoinSet so panics and errors surface
Finish in-flight requests and jobs on SIGTERM before exiting
Lay out the Cargo workspace: domain, data, web and binary crates
Bound concurrency with semaphores and bounded channels, never unbounded spawns
Size Tokio worker threads, the blocking pool and connection pools to the machine
Cut compile times with crate splits, a faster linker and fewer heavy macros
Propagate deadlines and keep work cancel-safe when the client disconnects
Find and stop memory growth: unbounded buffers, caches and allocator fragmentation

references.title: Monolith, modules, services and events
references.purpose: Read when laying out a new backend, choosing between one Axum binary for UI and API and a separate API service, drawing module boundaries, or deciding whether to extract a service or introduce events.

leaves.topic: Start as a modular monolith and extract services only on proven need
Serve UI and API from one Axum binary or split out a separate API service
Draw module boundaries around business capabilities with explicit interfaces
Keep business logic out of transport code so API, jobs and CLI share it
Type errors with thiserror, keep anyhow at the edges, map to responses once
Scale horizontally with stateless app servers and external session state
Decouple modules with events without creating a distributed monolith
Decide when to extract a service and define its contract and owner
Apply event sourcing or CQRS only where audit or read scale demands it

references.title: Consistency and concurrency across systems
references.purpose: Read when a workflow spans several steps or systems and must stay correct under retries, races and partial failure.

leaves.topic: Model workflows as explicit state machines with guarded transitions
Choose where strong consistency is required and where eventual is acceptable
Publish events atomically with the write using a transactional outbox
Avoid dual writes between the database and external systems
Write consumers that tolerate duplicate, reordered and delayed messages
Give users read-your-writes when reads lag behind writes
Orchestrate multi-step processes as a saga with compensations
Use distributed locks correctly, with expiry and fencing tokens
Write reconciliation jobs that check invariants across tables and systems

references.title: Multi-tenancy
references.purpose: Read when one deployment serves many customer organizations and their data and load must be kept apart, or tenants need their own settings, domain or region.

leaves.topic: Choose row, schema or database isolation for multi-tenancy
Model accounts, workspaces and users so one user can join many tenants
Scope every query, cache key, job and file path by tenant
Write tests proving cross-tenant reads and writes fail
Enforce tenant isolation with row-level security policies
Support per-tenant settings and overrides without forking the codebase
Limit noisy tenants with per-tenant quotas and fair scheduling
Serve customer custom domains with ownership verification and on-demand TLS certificates
Pin each tenant to a home region with isolated regional stacks and global routing
Move a large tenant to dedicated infrastructure without downtime

references.title: Background, scheduled and durable jobs
references.purpose: Read when work should happen outside the request: queues, retries, cron, long workflows, and stuck or duplicated jobs.

leaves.topic: Move slow work off the request path into background jobs
Write idempotent job handlers for at-least-once delivery
Start with a Postgres-backed queue and know when to outgrow it
Configure retries with backoff, jitter and a dead-letter queue
Run scheduled jobs exactly once across multiple instances
Set timeouts, concurrency limits and priorities per queue
Pass IDs, not payloads, and version job arguments across deploys
Alert on queue depth and age and scale workers to match
Orchestrate multi-step workflows with a durable execution engine
Drain or replay a poisoned queue without duplicating side effects

references.title: Realtime features
references.purpose: Read when the UI must update without a refresh: live status, chat, presence, collaboration or peer media.

leaves.topic: Choose polling, SSE, WebSockets or WebRTC for a realtime feature
Handle reconnects, missed messages and ordering on the client
Authenticate, authorize and rate-limit long-lived connections
Stream with Server-Sent Events, including reconnect and resume
Build presence, typing indicators and live cursors without flooding the server
Decide between a hosted realtime service and running your own
Scale WebSocket connections across instances with pub/sub
Build collaborative or offline-first features with a sync engine or CRDTs
Use WebRTC with STUN, TURN and a managed media server

references.title: File uploads and document processing
references.purpose: Read when users upload, import or export files, or the server must process images, video, CSV or PDFs.

leaves.topic: Upload directly to storage with presigned, size-limited requests
Restrict upload type and size and verify content, not the extension
Serve user files from a separate origin with safe content headers
Process images, video and documents in background jobs
Support resumable multipart uploads for large files and flaky networks
Import and export CSV with streaming, validation and row-level error reports
Generate PDFs and other documents server-side reliably
Scan uploads for malware and quarantine them before use

references.title: Third-party integrations and resilience
references.purpose: Read when calling an external API or another service, or when a dependency's failure spreads into your own outage.

leaves.topic: Set a timeout on every outbound call
Add jittered retries and circuit breakers to outbound calls
Degrade features gracefully when a third-party API is down
Wrap critical vendors behind an interface you can reimplement
Pin third-party API versions and test upgrades in a sandbox
Respect third-party rate limits with queues and token buckets
Store third-party OAuth tokens encrypted and refresh them before expiry
Shed load and apply backpressure so overload degrades gracefully
Stop retry storms with retry budgets and hedging limits
Build two-way syncs with external systems and resolve conflicts
